## Summary
This registrant is the German arm of Nokia Networks: the IEEE record for its 35 MA-L blocks (00:77:E4 from 2019, 60:A8:FE from 2014, 98:0A:4B from 2025) names "Nokia Solutions and Networks GmbH & Co. KG" at Werinherstrasse 91, Munich [1][2]. The business began on 1 April 2007 as Nokia Siemens Networks, a joint venture of Nokia and Siemens; Nokia bought out Siemens' half for EUR 1.7 billion in July 2013, renamed it Nokia Solutions and Networks, and folded it into the parent in 2014, keeping a Munich site [3][4]. Nokia Networks is Nokia's largest division, a data-networking and telecommunications-equipment business headquartered in Espoo that absorbed Alcatel-Lucent in 2016 and has since concentrated on 5G network apparatus [4][5]. What a MAC in one of these blocks is on a home or office network could not be pinned from the sources reached: every Nokia product page (nokia.com fixed-networks and Wi-Fi pages) returned HTTP 403, the OpenWrt and DeviWiki pages for Nokia consumer gateways do not exist, and the FCC ID mirrors returned 403, so device class, radios, silicon and FCC grantee are deliberately left unknown rather than filled from recollection. The operator should treat an address in this block as Nokia network equipment of some kind [4][5] and identify the model from the device itself (label, DHCP hostname, captive portal) rather than from this entry. No MAC-randomization behaviour and no vendor security advisories were found in the sources reached.
